summary: 1948 lookout on a 30-foot enclosed tower on private Santa Lucia Preserve land, named for a WWII forester; visits need the Preserve's permission.

facts.design: 16 by 16 ft octagonal cab on a 30 ft enclosed tower (NHLR); a lookout history site names it an 809R observation cab on a 30 ft enclosed tower

access.note: On private Santa Lucia Preserve land; access requires the Preserve's permission, and a locked gate guards the road.

visit.trail_note: Reached over private Preserve land by permission only; do not climb without permission.

Monterey County Planning Commission approved a telecommunications tower to be affixed to the lookout; construction not confirmed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 16 by 16 ft octagonal CalFire cab; the history site gives an 809R observation cab. Both put the 1948 cab on a 30-foot enclosed tower, so the model name is not settled.
A conservancy director's view that Ormsbee grew up living on the peak is not supported by the historical record, per the Monterey County Now article.

notes_for_editor: Record access 'unknown' can now read 'permission' (NHLR and Monterey County Now agree). The source_pages entry for a 2017 NYT article returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The OpenStreetMap way only tags the tower as an observation tower, so it is not cited. Staffing 'unstaffed as_of 2011' rests on the Peakbagging text; no source gives the year it was decommissioned (the article says 'sometime in the 1980s'), so no decommission event is recorded. Possible photo lead: archive.org item casbcfm_001261 (Sept 1955), licence not checked, not added.
